One envelope, every command

Answers an agent can act on.

Every command returns the same JSON shape on stdout, says where its data came from, and stays read-only until you decide otherwise.

  • ok / data / error / meta on every call, CLI or MCP
  • readOnly reported, not assumed
  • source on every result, so nothing is a mystery
Preview · planned output
~/orders-service 
$ npx -y @imagile-dev/toil db query --connection reporting "select status, count(*) from orders group by status"
{  "ok": true,  "data": {    "columns": ["status", "count"],    "rows": [["open", 42], ["shipped", 318]],    "truncated": false  },  "meta": { "source": "postgres:reporting", "readOnly": true }}

Built for the locked-down laptop

If your machine runs Node, it runs toil.

Application control blocks unsigned executables. Security reviews stall on native modules. toil is built so there is nothing for either to catch.

  • No executable

    One bundled JavaScript file on the Node you already have. Nothing for application control to block.

  • No install scripts

    No postinstall, no native addon, no binary download. It installs cleanly with --ignore-scripts.

  • No browser login

    Paste a token you generated once. No OAuth dance, no SSO pop-up, no device code.

  • No telemetry

    toil talks only to hosts in your config. Your firewall logs show exactly what you expect.

The central integrator

One switchboard for everything outside the editor.

Your agent asks toil, and toil knows which line to plug in. Databases and every enterprise tool sit behind one interface and one JSON shape, so nothing new to learn per system.

db

Databases

List connections, describe tables, preview rows and run queries with paging and a row cap, against PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, SQLite and Oracle. Read-only unless you say otherwise.

$ toil db describe-table orders --connection reporting
tools

Enterprise tools

Issue trackers, source hosts, CI, scanners and observability, each behind one pasted token and one consistent JSON shape.

$ toil jira get-issue --key PAY-1042

MCP, without the approval queue

Stand in for the server you can't install.

Vendor MCP servers are often blocked, need a browser login, or don't exist. Scope toil to the areas you need and point your agent at it: one config entry, a small, focused tool list, and write tools that only exist if you've turned them on.

mcp.json 

  "mcpServers": 
    "tickets-and-docs": 
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y", "@imagile-dev/toil", "mcp",
        "--areas", "jira,confluence"
      ]

How it's built

Principles first. Rules follow.

Every decision in toil traces back to a short list of principles. Here are the first three.

  1. 01

    Adoptable inside a locked-down enterprise

    The only things your security team approves are Node and one npm package.

  2. 02

    Safe by default when an agent is driving

    An agent cannot discover a write tool you have not turned on.

  3. 03

    One command, one source; you compose

    You always know which system a result came from, and you choose which ones to ask.
